texto.periodico: Journal of Coastal Archaeology and Geochronology (2026) 11(2), 141–168
texto.titulo: Shell, charcoal and sand: a multi-method chronology for the Ponta da Corvina shell midden, southern Brazil
texto.autores: C. Arendt-Paiva, T. Mwangi-Sobral and L. Hesketh-Moura
texto.abstract: Shell middens are among the most conspicuous archaeological features of the southern Brazilian coast, yet the ages assigned to many of them rest on single radiocarbon dates obtained decades ago on marine shell and reported without calibration or correction. This study re-examined the chronology of the Ponta da Corvina midden, a mound whose basal date of 7,180 ± 120 radiocarbon years BP has long been cited as evidence that it is the oldest on this stretch of coast. Radiocarbon dates on marine shell and on charcoal from the same stratigraphic contexts were compared, optically stimulated luminescence (OSL) ages were obtained on the sands underlying and overlying the mound, and all results were integrated in a Bayesian model constrained by the order of the layers. Forty-six samples were collected from eleven anthropogenic layers and the adjacent sands. Uncorrected shell dates were on average 540 years older than charcoal from the same contexts; once a regional marine reservoir correction was applied, 12 of the 14 pairs (86%) were statistically consistent. The model places the onset of shell accumulation at 5,640–5,450 cal BP and its end at 3,910–3,760 cal BP. The earlier basal date is best explained by a natural shell bed beneath the mound, combined with the absence of a reservoir correction.
texto.keywords: radiocarbon dating, marine reservoir effect, optically stimulated luminescence, Bayesian chronological modelling, shell midden, stratigraphy

blocos.p: Few questions in archaeology are as basic, or as consequential, as the question of when. Whether two sites were occupied at the same time, or how quickly a settlement grew, cannot be established without a chronology, and a chronology is only as sound as the dates on which it rests. Along the southern coast of Brazil, this problem is posed with particular force by the sambaquis, mounds built largely of mollusc shells, sediment, charcoal and, in many cases, human burials, some of which reach heights of more than 20 m. These structures were accumulated over centuries by fishing and gathering communities, and their ages have been used to reconstruct the timing of coastal settlement, the evolution of lagoon environments and the emergence of monumental building practices (Rocha-Vinterberg, 2006; Saldanha and Prew, 2013). Yet many of the dates on which those reconstructions depend were obtained decades ago, often from a single sample, and are reported in ways that make them difficult to compare with modern results.

The Ponta da Corvina midden illustrates the difficulty. In the first systematic investigation of the site, Albuquerque-Steen (1987) obtained a radiocarbon date of 7,180 ± 120 years BP on shells collected from the base of the quarry face and concluded that the mound was the oldest on this stretch of coast, predating its neighbours by more than a millennium. The figure was widely cited. Tessaro and Moyle (2004), however, questioned not the measurement but its interpretation: because the date had been obtained on marine shell and reported in radiocarbon years, without calibration or correction for the marine reservoir effect, it overstated the age of the deposit, in their estimate by several centuries. Ferreira-Lund (2009) went further, suggesting that the dated shells might not have been discarded by people at all, since natural shell beds formed by storm waves are common in the sands on which many middens rest; in that case, the date would refer to the beach on which the mound was later built rather than to the mound itself.

The debate has also extended to the other material commonly dated at such sites. Brandão-Kell (2011) warned that charcoal-based chronologies, often preferred precisely because they avoid the complications of marine carbon, may themselves make sites appear older than they are, as the builders of shell mounds burned driftwood and the trunks of long-lived trees whose inner rings could have grown centuries before the fires were lit. Okafor-Duarte (2018), for her part, drew attention to a different source of error: in many sambaquis, the upper layers have been disturbed by twentieth-century lime quarrying, by earlier excavations and by burrowing crabs, so that the order of the layers in the upper part of a mound cannot be taken at face value. Taken together, these studies suggest that each of the methods applied to sambaquis is open to a specific bias, and that the direction of each bias differs.

Despite this debate, no study has so far dated the same contexts in a single midden with more than one material and method and then combined the results in a formal model. Most revisions of sambaqui chronologies have recalibrated published dates rather than collecting new samples (Saldanha and Prew, 2013), and those which have collected new samples have usually relied on a single material. The present study addresses this gap. By dating marine shell and charcoal from the same contexts, by obtaining luminescence ages on the sands below and above the Ponta da Corvina midden and by combining all dates with the stratigraphic sequence, it seeks both to establish when the mound was built and to assess how far each of the biases discussed above affects the dating of shell middens more generally. Such a study matters beyond a single site: if the age of the mound most often cited as the oldest on this coast turns out to be inflated, the regional models of settlement that take it as their starting point would have to be reconsidered as well.

Archaeological dating methods fall into two broad groups. Relative methods place deposits or objects in order without assigning them an age in years, and the most fundamental of them is the principle of superposition: in a sequence of layers that has not been disturbed, each layer is younger than the one beneath it and older than the one above. Stratigraphy, the description and interpretation of such layers, therefore provides an order, but it does not reveal how much time separates one layer from the next. Absolute methods, by contrast, yield numerical ages, usually with a stated margin of uncertainty. The two are complementary rather than competing: numerical ages anchor the stratigraphic sequence in time, while the sequence, in turn, allows ages that are inconsistent with the order of deposition to be identified (Lindqvist-Amaral, 2012). In a shell midden, however, the assumption that deposition proceeded in an orderly way from bottom to top has to be checked rather than taken for granted, because later digging and burrowing animals can move material from one layer to another.

Radiocarbon dating, the absolute method most widely applied to archaeological sites, rests on a simple principle. Carbon-14, a radioactive form of carbon, is produced continuously in the upper atmosphere and enters living organisms through photosynthesis and the food chain, so that, while an organism is alive, the proportion of carbon-14 in its tissues remains roughly in equilibrium with that of its environment. When the organism dies, the uptake stops, and the carbon-14 it contains decays at a known rate, with a half-life of about 5,730 years. Measuring the proportion that remains therefore indicates how long ago death occurred. After about 50,000 years, so little carbon-14 is left that it can no longer be reliably distinguished from contamination, which sets the practical limit of the method. Radiocarbon ages are not, however, calendar ages: because the concentration of carbon-14 in the atmosphere has varied over time, a raw radiocarbon age has to be converted into a calendar age by calibration. Calibration curves are constructed from materials of independently known age, above all tree rings, and calibrated ages are conventionally reported as years “cal BP”, that is, calendar years before AD 1950.

blocos.h3: Reservoir effects, old wood and other materials

blocos.p: Two complications are particularly relevant to shell middens. The first concerns marine organisms. Carbon dissolved in the ocean exchanges only slowly with the atmosphere, and the deep water that rises to the surface offshore may have been isolated from it for centuries. Because carbon dissolved in the deep ocean has been cut off from the atmosphere for so long, marine organisms incorporate carbon that is already depleted in carbon-14, which makes them appear several hundred years older than terrestrial organisms that died at the same moment. This offset, known as the marine reservoir effect, averages roughly 400 years worldwide, but its local magnitude varies with ocean currents, upwelling and freshwater input; the local deviation from the global average is expressed as ΔR and must be estimated for each region (Nakamura-Reis, 2015). The second complication concerns charcoal. A radiocarbon date on wood charcoal indicates when the wood grew, not when it was burned, and the inner rings of a long-lived tree may be centuries older than the fire in which they ended up. This so-called old-wood effect can be avoided only by dating short-lived materials, such as twigs, seeds or nutshells. Bone, the third material commonly found in middens, can be dated through its collagen, but collagen is often poorly preserved in warm, humid settings.

blocos.h3: Luminescence, tree rings and Bayesian modelling

blocos.p: Methods that do not depend on carbon offer independent checks. Optically stimulated luminescence (OSL) dates the last time that grains of quartz or feldspar in a sediment were exposed to sunlight. Once buried, grains accumulate energy from the natural radiation of the surrounding sediment; in the laboratory, this energy is released by light as a measurable signal, and dividing the absorbed dose by the annual dose rate gives the time elapsed since burial. OSL can be applied to sediments containing no organic material and well beyond the range of radiocarbon, but its uncertainties, typically 5 to 10% of the age, are larger. Dendrochronology, which matches patterns of wide and narrow annual tree rings against a regional reference sequence, can date wood to the calendar year, but it requires well-preserved timber and a long master chronology, neither of which is available for most coastal sites in the region; its principal contribution to the present study is thus indirect, through the tree-ring records that underpin radiocarbon calibration. Finally, Bayesian chronological modelling combines dates with prior information, most often the stratigraphic order, to produce estimates that are more precise than the individual dates and to calculate quantities, such as the start, end and duration of a phase, that no single date can provide (Lindqvist-Amaral, 2012).

The study was guided by four research questions: (1) To what extent do radiocarbon dates on marine shell and on charcoal from the same stratigraphic contexts differ, and is the difference accounted for by the marine reservoir effect once a local ΔR correction is applied? (2) Are OSL ages on the sands beneath and above the midden consistent with the radiocarbon chronology? (3) When did shell accumulation begin and end, and over how long a period was the site used, once all dates are combined with the stratigraphic sequence in a Bayesian model? (4) To what extent have bioturbation and earlier excavations disturbed the upper layers, and which dates should consequently be treated as unreliable?

The Ponta da Corvina midden lies on a sandy promontory on the northern shore of the Taquarema lagoon, a shallow coastal lagoon connected to the sea by a narrow inlet. The mound, which formerly rose some 12 m above the lagoon shore, now reaches about 9 m, its southern half having been removed by lime quarrying in the 1950s. Fieldwork was carried out in two seasons, in 2023 and 2024. A trench measuring 2 × 3 m was cut into the northern flank, which had been left untouched by the quarrying, and was taken down to sterile sand at a depth of 9.4 m. Eleven anthropogenic layers were distinguished on the basis of colour, texture and shell content and numbered from the top (Layer 1) to the base (Layer 11). The layers rested on a beach sand (Unit S0), within which a horizon of densely packed, unbroken and unburned shells was recorded about 0.6 m below the base of Layer 11, and they were capped by up to 1.1 m of wind-blown dune sand (Unit S12). A backfilled pit, which must have been dug after the 1950s, since its fill contained fragments of plastic, was identified in the western section of the trench, where it cut through Layers 2 to 5.

A total of 46 samples were collected: 18 of marine shell, 16 of charcoal, 6 of bone and 6 for OSL. Sixteen shell samples were taken from the anthropogenic layers and two from the natural shell horizon in Unit S0. Each shell sample consisted of a single articulated bivalve of one estuarine species, so that every dated shell could be assumed to represent an individual that had died shortly before deposition. Because charcoal was distributed unevenly through the sequence, paired shell and charcoal samples from the same context could be obtained in only 14 cases. Wherever possible, charcoal fragments from short-lived twigs were preferred to those from trunk wood; seven of the 16 charcoal samples were identified as twigs, and the remaining nine as trunk wood of long-lived species. The six OSL samples were collected by hammering opaque steel tubes into the cleaned section, three in Unit S0 and three in Unit S12, and were opened at the laboratory under subdued red light.

Radiocarbon measurements were made by accelerator mass spectrometry at the Meridian Radiocarbon Facility. In the standard procedure applied there to shell, the outer surface of each valve is removed by acid etching, which eliminates carbon that may have been exchanged with groundwater, and X-ray diffraction is used to confirm that the original aragonite has not recrystallised; charcoal was treated with a sequence of acid, alkali and acid washes to remove carbonates and humic contaminants. Bone samples were submitted for collagen extraction, but in all six cases the collagen yield fell below the 1% threshold that the laboratory requires, and they were excluded from further analysis. OSL measurements were made on quartz grains at the Halvard Luminescence Laboratory. Charcoal dates were calibrated with the Southern Hemisphere atmospheric curve and shell dates with the marine curve, applying a regional ΔR of 95 ± 45 years (Nakamura-Reis, 2015).

All radiocarbon and OSL results were then combined in a Bayesian model in which the eleven layers were treated as a sequence of phases, bounded below by the OSL ages on Unit S0 and above by those on Unit S12. An outlier model was applied so that dates inconsistent with their stratigraphic position would be down-weighted rather than arbitrarily removed, and the fit between the model and the dates was assessed with an agreement index, values below 60% being taken to indicate a poor fit. Two versions of the model were run: one including all dates and one in which the dates from Layers 1 to 3 were excluded, so that the effect of the disturbance identified in the upper layers could be evaluated. Before modelling, each pair of shell and charcoal dates from the same context was tested for consistency at the 95% level; pairs that passed the test were combined before being entered into the model, whereas pairs that failed it were entered as separate dates.

The upper three layers showed clear signs of disturbance. Fragments of glass and iron were found in Layers 1 and 2, crab burrows filled with darker sediment were recorded throughout Layers 1 to 3, and the backfilled pit in the western section had mixed material from Layers 2 to 5. These observations were matched by the dates. Of the nine radiocarbon dates from Layers 1 to 3, three (33%) were inconsistent with their stratigraphic position, the most striking being a charcoal date from Layer 2 that was older than every date from Layer 5. In contrast, only one of the 23 dates from Layers 4 to 11 (4%) was out of sequence, and it came from a sample taken close to the edge of the backfilled pit. The disturbance was not uniform across the trench, however: in the eastern section, away from the pit, Layers 2 and 3 retained sharp boundaries, although crab burrows were present there as well.

Shell and charcoal dates from the same contexts differed systematically. Before correction, the shell dates were older than the paired charcoal dates in all 14 cases, by a mean of 540 years (range 310–890). Once the shell dates had been calibrated with the marine curve and the regional ΔR, the mean difference fell to 115 years, and 12 of the 14 pairs (86%) were statistically consistent at the 95% level. Among the 14 pairs, the charcoal had been identified as twigs in seven and as trunk wood in seven; after correction, the mean offsets from the shell dates were 40 and 190 years, respectively. The two pairs that failed the test were both trunk-wood ones, and in each of them the charcoal was older than the shell, by 260 years in Layer 7 and by 330 years in Layer 9; such a pattern is what the old-wood effect would lead one to expect.

The OSL ages were consistent with the radiocarbon chronology. In Unit S0, the sample taken beside the natural shell horizon yielded an age of 7.5 ± 0.5 ka, and the two samples taken immediately beneath Layer 11 yielded 6.0 ± 0.4 and 5.8 ± 0.4 ka. The two shells from the natural horizon gave radiocarbon ages of 7,240 ± 40 and 7,090 ± 40 BP, which, once calibrated with the marine curve and ΔR, correspond to 7,680–7,480 and 7,560–7,360 cal BP, in close agreement with the adjacent OSL age. In Unit S12, the three samples yielded 3.9 ± 0.3, 3.5 ± 0.3 and 3.2 ± 0.2 ka, the oldest of them coming from the base of the dune sand, where it rested against the upper flank of the mound. Because this age overlaps the modelled ages of Layers 4 and 5, it appears that dune sand had been accumulating against the landward side of the mound for some time before shell deposition ceased.

tabela.nota: Note. Shell dates calibrated with the marine curve and ΔR = 95 ± 45 years; charcoal dates with the Southern Hemisphere atmospheric curve. Differences are between the midpoints of the paired ranges; negative values indicate that the charcoal is older than the shell. Preferred model (Layers 1–3 excluded): start of shell accumulation 5,640–5,450 cal BP; end 3,910–3,760 cal BP; agreement index 74%.

blocos.p: Table 1 shows, for four of the paired contexts and for the sands that bracket the mound, the calibrated age ranges obtained on each material, the difference between the paired shell and charcoal dates and the OSL ages; the boundaries estimated by the preferred model, from which the dates from Layers 1 to 3 were excluded, are given in the note. The overall agreement index of that model was 74%, above the 60% threshold, whereas the model that included Layers 1 to 3 yielded an index of only 41%. Layer 11, the oldest reliably dated charcoal-bearing layer in the sequence, was modelled to 5,580–5,410 cal BP, and the start of shell accumulation was placed at 5,640–5,450 cal BP. The end of accumulation was placed at 3,910–3,760 cal BP, and the model estimated the duration of use at between 1,560 and 1,860 years. The rate of accumulation was not constant: the lower six layers, which together account for 5.6 m of the deposit, accumulated within roughly 600 years, and the remaining 3.8 m accumulated rather slowly over more than a millennium.

The first research question concerned the offset between shell and charcoal. Most of this offset is accounted for by the marine reservoir effect, and the residual difference was concentrated in pairs involving trunk wood. Shells have often been regarded as the less trustworthy of the two materials, on the grounds that the origin of their carbon is uncertain (Rocha-Vinterberg, 2006). The present data point in the opposite direction. A bivalve lives for only a few years and was, in all likelihood, eaten and discarded soon after it was collected; yet it is precisely this material that sambaqui researchers have tended to distrust. Charcoal from trunk wood, conversely, may incorporate carbon fixed decades or centuries before the fire, and twig charcoal, though free of this problem, is scarce in most middens. When a reliable ΔR value is available, then, articulated shells may be the more dependable of the two materials.

These results also help to resolve the controversy over the age of the site. The two shells from the natural horizon in Unit S0 returned radiocarbon ages almost identical to the 7,180 ± 120 BP reported by Albuquerque-Steen (1987), and the OSL age from the same horizon places it about two millennia before the onset of the midden. It therefore seems likely that the shells dated in 1987, collected at the base of the quarry face, belonged to this natural horizon rather than to the anthropogenic layers, as Ferreira-Lund (2009) suspected. This is not to say that the original measurement was flawed; indeed, its accuracy is scarcely in doubt, since it has now been reproduced on two independent samples. What was mistaken was the inference drawn from it, and the error was compounded by the absence of a reservoir correction, the point on which Tessaro and Moyle (2004) had insisted. Even so, neither explanation alone would account for the full discrepancy: the reservoir correction removes about five centuries, whereas the gap between the 1987 date and the onset of the midden is considerably wider.

The second and third research questions concerned the agreement between methods and the overall chronology. The OSL ages bracket the radiocarbon sequence closely: the sands beneath Layer 11 were last exposed to light around 6,000 years ago, and the base of the dune sand was buried while shells were still being deposited on the mound. The radiocarbon dates are far more precise than the OSL ages, whereas the OSL ages have the advantage of being entirely independent of carbon and, therefore, of both the reservoir and the old-wood effects. In the Bayesian model, that independence matters more than precision. The model indicates that the mound was built over some 1,700 years, rapidly at first and more slowly later, a pattern which Saldanha and Prew (2013) observed at two other sambaquis around the lagoon and attributed to the gradual silting of the inlet, which would have reduced the availability of estuarine shellfish. The rapid early phase would also coincide with the period in which the lagoon was most open to the sea, although the present data cannot test this explanation directly.

The fourth research question concerned disturbance, and here the results carry a warning that extends well beyond this site. A model that included the upper three layers fitted the data poorly. Had these layers been sampled alone, as the upper parts of mounds frequently are in rescue excavations, the resulting chronology would have been seriously distorted. More generally, the findings imply that the regional databases on which reconstructions of coastal settlement rely contain many dates whose meaning is uncertain: single uncorrected shell dates, charcoal dates on unidentified wood and dates from the upper layers of disturbed mounds. Such dates need to be recalibrated with an appropriate ΔR and, where possible, checked against independent evidence before they are used to argue that one site is older than another. The same caution applies to dates obtained decades ago on samples whose stratigraphic position was recorded only approximately, as was the case for the 1987 date.

Several limitations should be noted. First, the ΔR value applied was regional rather than specific to the Taquarema lagoon, and in estuarine settings the offset may vary with the amount of freshwater input, which could itself have changed as the inlet silted up. Second, only one trench was excavated, and although it was placed in the best-preserved part of the mound, the sequence it exposed may not be representative of the whole structure, whose southern half has been lost. Third, no bone could be dated, so the chronology of the burials that sambaquis frequently contain remains unknown at this site. Finally, the charcoal fragments were too small, and no regional tree-ring sequence is long enough, for dendrochronology to be applied directly to the wood burned at the site.

Future research could address several of these issues. A local ΔR value could be obtained by dating shells of known collection date held in museum collections gathered from the lagoon before nuclear weapons testing altered atmospheric carbon-14 in the 1950s. Where charcoal is used, efforts should be concentrated on short-lived materials such as twigs, seeds and nutshells, which the present results suggest are far less prone to error than trunk wood. Single-grain OSL dating of the shell-bearing sediment itself, rather than of the sands that bracket it, might provide an independent age for each layer and show whether grains from different layers have been mixed. Finally, applying the same multi-method approach to the other middens around the lagoon would make it possible to determine whether the pattern of rapid early growth and slower later accumulation is a regional phenomenon.

This study has shown that the Ponta da Corvina midden is considerably younger than has long been claimed. Shell accumulation began between 5,640 and 5,450 cal BP and ended between 3,910 and 3,760 cal BP; the basal date of 7,180 BP, far from marking the arrival of the mound builders, almost certainly records a natural shell bed formed some two millennia earlier. Marine shell, once corrected for the reservoir effect, proved at least as reliable as charcoal, and the main source of error in the charcoal dates was the burning of long-lived wood. No single method, however, would have been sufficient: it was only by dating different materials from the same contexts, by checking them against luminescence ages and by combining all of them with the stratigraphic order that the biases of each method could be identified. The chronologies of other shell middens, many of which rest on a single uncorrected date, should be revisited in the same way.

questoes.explicacao:
O resumo diz o que foi feito: Radiocarbon dates on marine shell and on charcoal from the same stratigraphic contexts were compared, optically stimulated luminescence (OSL) ages were obtained on the sands underlying and overlying the mound, and all results were integrated in a Bayesian model constrained by the order of the layers. O título confirma o recorte: a multi-method chronology for the Ponta da Corvina shell midden, um único sítio. Só (c) mantém todos os elementos.

Cada distrator troca uma peça. (a) troca carvão por ossos: houve amostras de osso, mas nenhuma pôde ser datada (§12). (b) põe a luminescência nas conchas; ela foi feita nas areias abaixo e acima do sambaqui (on the sands underlying and overlying the mound). (d) amplia para “os sambaquis de uma laguna”: os outros sítios da laguna só aparecem como literatura e como pesquisa futura. (e) inverte o papel da estratigrafia: o modelo é constrained by the order of the layers, isto é, depende dela.
questoes.dica: Dica: separe o que o resumo diz sobre o objeto (um sítio ou vários?), os materiais (concha, carvão, osso, areia) e o papel de cada método. Compare as alternativas palavra por palavra com a frase que descreve o que foi feito; a diferença costuma estar em um só termo (carvão × ossos, areias × conchas, respeita × dispensa).

questoes.enunciado:
Na introdução (§2–§3), os autores retomam estudos anteriores sobre a idade do sítio e sobre a datação de sambaquis. Associe as colunas, relacionando cada afirmação a seu(s) respectivo(s) autor(es). Um dos autores não será utilizado.

  1. Albuquerque-Steen (1987)
  2. Tessaro and Moyle (2004)
  3. Ferreira-Lund (2009)
  4. Brandão-Kell (2011)
  5. Okafor-Duarte (2018)
  • (  )A data mais antiga talvez nem diga respeito ao sambaqui, já que as conchas datadas podem ter se acumulado naturalmente, antes de qualquer ocupação humana.
  • (  )O problema da data não estava na medição, mas na leitura que se fez dela: por ser de concha marinha e não ter sido corrigida, ela exagerava a idade do depósito.
  • (  )O material costumeiramente preferido por evitar as complicações do carbono marinho também pode fazer os sítios parecerem mais antigos do que são.
  • (  )Nos níveis superiores de muitos sambaquis, a sequência das camadas não merece confiança automática, pois foi revolvida por mineração, escavações e animais.

Assinale a sequência correta.

Sobra Albuquerque-Steen (1), que obteve a data e concluiu que o sítio era o mais antigo da costa; ele não fez nenhuma das críticas.

Nas alternativas erradas: (b) erra os itens 2 e 4; (c) erra os itens 1, 2, 3 e 4; (d) erra os itens 1, 2 e 3; (e) erra o item 4.
questoes.dica: Dica: quando vários autores discutem o mesmo assunto (a mesma data), o tema não basta: identifique a posição de cada um (quem produziu o dado, quem questionou a interpretação, quem questionou a origem da amostra). Desconfie do autor “óbvio” do parágrafo: ele pode ser justamente o que sobra.

questoes.enunciado: Os segmentos sublinhados em “Because carbon dissolved in the deep ocean has been cut off from the atmosphere for so long, marine organisms incorporate carbon that is already depleted in carbon-14, which makes them appear several hundred years older than terrestrial organisms that died at the same moment. This offset, known as the marine reservoir effect, averages roughly 400 years worldwide, but its local magnitude varies with ocean currents, upwelling and freshwater input” (§7) referem-se, respectivamente, a
alternativas: carbon-14 – marine organisms – a diferença de idade aparente entre organismos marinhos e terrestres que morreram juntos – the deep ocean.

o fato de os organismos marinhos incorporarem carbono já empobrecido em carbono-14 – terrestrial organisms – a diferença de idade aparente entre organismos marinhos e terrestres que morreram juntos – the marine reservoir effect.
carbon-14 – terrestrial organisms – o longo isolamento do carbono do oceano profundo em relação à atmosfera – the deep ocean.

o fato de os organismos marinhos incorporarem carbono já empobrecido em carbono-14 – marine organisms – a diferença de idade aparente entre organismos marinhos e terrestres que morreram juntos – the marine reservoir effect.
carbon-14 – marine organisms – o longo isolamento do carbono do oceano profundo em relação à atmosfera – the deep ocean.
questoes.explicacao:
which: depois de vírgula e seguido de makes, retoma a oração inteira anterior: é o fato de os organismos incorporarem carbono empobrecido que os “faz parecer” mais velhos.

them: quem parece várias centenas de anos mais velho são os organismos marinhos, comparados than terrestrial organisms.

This offset: offset = “defasagem”, “desvio”; resume a diferença de idade aparente que acabou de ser descrita, e por isso recebe o nome de marine reservoir effect.

its: a magnitude local que varia com correntes e ressurgência é a do efeito reservatório, sujeito da oração.

Nas alternativas erradas: (a) erra os itens 1 e 4; (b) erra o item 2; (c) erra os itens 1, 2, 3 e 4; (e) erra os itens 1, 3 e 4.
questoes.dica: Método: (1) which após vírgula seguido de verbo como makes, means, suggests costuma retomar a oração toda (“o que faz…”); (2) para them, teste cada candidato plural no verbo (“faz os organismos marinhos parecerem mais velhos”?) e lembre que o termo de comparação (than X) não é o referente; (3) this + substantivo resume a ideia anterior: pergunte qual ideia pode ser chamada de “defasagem”; (4) para its, procure o sujeito da oração.

questoes.enunciado: Os parágrafos 1 a 8, que antecedem a seção de método, estão organizados, em termos de conteúdo, em diferentes partes, as quais são
alternativas: a importância das datas e o problema das cronologias de sambaquis (§1); a lacuna e o objetivo do estudo (§2); o debate sobre a idade do sítio e os vieses de cada material e método (§3–§4); os fundamentos dos métodos de datação (§5–§8).

a importância das datas e o problema das cronologias de sambaquis (§1); o debate sobre a idade do sítio e os vieses de cada material e método (§2–§3); os fundamentos dos métodos de datação (§4–§7); as hipóteses do estudo (§8).

a importância das datas e o problema das cronologias de sambaquis (§1); o debate sobre a idade do sítio e os vieses dos métodos (§2–§3); a lacuna e o objetivo (§4); um estudo-piloto no sítio (§5–§6); os fundamentos dos métodos (§7–§8).

a importância das datas e o problema das cronologias de sambaquis (§1); o debate sobre a idade do sítio e os vieses de cada material e método (§2–§3); a lacuna e o objetivo do estudo (§4); os fundamentos dos métodos de datação (§5–§8).

a importância das datas e o problema das cronologias de sambaquis (§1); o debate sobre a idade do sítio e os vieses de cada material e método (§2–§3); os fundamentos dos métodos de datação (§4–§7); a lacuna e o objetivo do estudo (§8).
questoes.explicacao:
(d) segue a ordem real. O §1 apresenta o problema geral: a chronology is only as sound as the dates on which it rests, e muitas datas de sambaquis were obtained decades ago, often from a single sample. Os §2–§3 retomam o debate: a data de 7.180 BP e as críticas de Tessaro e Moyle e de Ferreira-Lund (§2), depois os vieses do carvão e da perturbação das camadas (§3), fechando com each of the methods applied to sambaquis is open to a specific bias. O §4 aponta a lacuna e o objetivo: no study has so far dated the same contexts […]; The present study addresses this gap. Os §5–§8, sob os subtítulos de datação relativa e absoluta, radiocarbono, efeito reservatório e luminescência, explicam os métodos.

(a) inverte a ordem: põe a lacuna e o objetivo no §2, quando o §2 trata da data de 1987 e das críticas a ela; o objetivo só aparece no §4.

(b) inclui uma parte que não existe: o §8 não apresenta hipóteses, mas a luminescência, a dendrocronologia e a modelagem bayesiana. Além disso, o §4 não explica métodos.

(c) inventa um “estudo-piloto” nos §5–§6. Esses parágrafos explicam a datação relativa e absoluta e o radiocarbono; não há resultados preliminares do sítio na introdução.

(e) é a leitura apressada de quem espera o objetivo no fim da introdução, como em muitos artigos. Aqui ele vem no §4, antes da parte conceitual; o §8 começa com Methods that do not depend on carbon offer independent checks.
questoes.dica: Dica: resuma cada parágrafo em três ou quatro palavras e só depois compare com as alternativas. Use os subtítulos e as frases de abertura (The present study addresses this gap, Archaeological dating methods fall into two broad groups) como marcos. Desconfie de partes “típicas” de artigo (hipóteses, estudo-piloto) que o texto não tem, e da ordem que você espera encontrar em vez da ordem que o texto segue.

questoes.enunciado: Assinale a alternativa que NÃO corresponde a nenhuma das perguntas de pesquisa do estudo (§9).
alternativas: Medir quanto divergem as datas de conchas e de carvão de um mesmo contexto e verificar se a correção local do efeito reservatório explica essa divergência.
Verificar se as idades por luminescência das areias situadas sob e sobre o sambaqui são compatíveis com a cronologia obtida pelo radiocarbono.
Estimar quando o acúmulo de conchas começou e terminou e por quanto tempo o sítio foi usado, combinando as datas com a sequência das camadas.
Avaliar em que medida a ação de organismos e escavações anteriores revolveu as camadas superiores e quais datas devem ser tratadas como pouco confiáveis.
Verificar se as datas obtidas em fragmentos de osso concordam com as de carvão e de conchas retiradas das mesmas camadas do sambaqui.
questoes.explicacao:
As quatro perguntas do §9 aparecem parafraseadas em (a) = (1) To what extent do radiocarbon dates on marine shell and on charcoal from the same stratigraphic contexts differ, and is the difference accounted for by the marine reservoir effect once a local ΔR correction is applied?; (b) = (2) Are OSL ages on the sands beneath and above the midden consistent with the radiocarbon chronology?; (c) = (3) When did shell accumulation begin and end, and over how long a period was the site used […]?; (d) = (4) To what extent have bioturbation and earlier excavations disturbed the upper layers, and which dates should consequently be treated as unreliable? (“ação de organismos” = bioturbation).

(e) é o intruso, e soa familiar porque o estudo de fato coletou seis amostras de osso (§11). Mas o osso não entra em nenhuma pergunta de pesquisa, e as amostras nem chegaram a ser datadas: in all six cases the collagen yield fell below the 1% threshold […], and they were excluded from further analysis (§12).
questoes.dica: Dica: em “NÃO corresponde”, marque cada alternativa com o número da pergunta, mesmo que esteja parafraseada (bioturbation = revolvimento por organismos). O intruso costuma ser algo que o estudo menciona em outra seção, como uma amostra coletada ou um resultado secundário, e por isso parece fazer parte do desenho.

questoes.enunciado:
Sobre o método do estudo, indique se os segmentos a seguir estão em acordo (A) ou desacordo (D) com o que apresentam os parágrafos 10 a 12.

  • (  )Das 46 amostras coletadas, as de concha eram mais numerosas que as de carvão e as de luminescência somadas.
  • (  )Nenhuma das amostras de osso chegou a ser datada, porque todas renderam menos colágeno do que o laboratório exigia.
  • (  )Deu-se preferência, sempre que possível, ao carvão de galhos finos, mas estes responderam por menos da metade das amostras de carvão.
  • (  )A trincheira foi aberta no flanco que a extração de cal havia poupado, mas foi encerrada antes de atingir a areia estéril.

Assinale a sequência correta.
alternativas: A – A – A – A
D – A – A – D
D – D – A – D
A – D – D – A
A – A – D – A
questoes.explicacao:
1 (D): A total of 46 samples were collected: 18 of marine shell, 16 of charcoal, 6 of bone and 6 for OSL (§11). Concha (18) é o maior grupo isolado, mas carvão + luminescência somam 22. É preciso fazer a conta.

2 (A): in all six cases the collagen yield fell below the 1% threshold that the laboratory requires, and they were excluded from further analysis (§12).

3 (A): Wherever possible, charcoal fragments from short-lived twigs were preferred to those from trunk wood; seven of the 16 charcoal samples were identified as twigs (§11): 7 de 16 é menos da metade.

4 (D): a primeira parte está certa (the northern flank, which had been left untouched by the quarrying), mas a trincheira was taken down to sterile sand at a depth of 9.4 m (§10), ou seja, chegou à areia estéril.

Cada alternativa errada difere da certa em um único item; é preciso conferir os quatro.

Nas alternativas erradas: (a) erra os itens 1 e 4; (c) erra o item 2; (d) erra os itens 1, 2, 3 e 4; (e) erra os itens 1, 3 e 4.
questoes.dica: Dica: quando o item compara quantidades (“mais numerosas que … somadas”, “menos da metade”), faça a conta com os números do texto. Em itens com duas partes ligadas por “mas”, confira as duas: é comum a primeira estar certa e a segunda trocar um detalhe (chegou × não chegou à areia estéril).

questoes.enunciado:
Considere os segmentos a seguir.

I - “A trench measuring 2 × 3 m was cut into the northern flank, which had been left untouched by the quarrying” (§10)II - “In the standard procedure applied there to shell, the outer surface of each valve is removed by acid etching” (§12)III - “it appears that dune sand had been accumulating against the landward side of the mound for some time before shell deposition ceased” (§16)

Os segmentos sublinhados estão, respectivamente, nos seguintes tempos e vozes verbais:
alternativas: passado perfeito, voz passiva – presente simples, voz passiva – passado perfeito contínuo, voz passiva.
passado perfeito, voz ativa – presente simples, voz ativa – passado perfeito contínuo, voz passiva.
passado perfeito, voz passiva – presente simples, voz passiva – passado perfeito contínuo, voz ativa.
passado perfeito, voz ativa – presente simples, voz passiva – passado perfeito contínuo, voz ativa.
passado perfeito, voz ativa – presente simples, voz ativa – passado perfeito contínuo, voz ativa.
questoes.explicacao:
I had been left: had (passado perfeito) + been + particípio (left) = passado perfeito, voz passiva: o flanco “tinha sido deixado” intacto pela extração, antes da escavação. Não é presente perfeito, que usaria has been left; nem ativa, porque há be + particípio.

II is removed: is + particípio = presente simples, voz passiva (a superfície “é removida”). O presente aqui descreve um procedimento padrão, geral, e não um evento do passado.

III had been accumulating: had been + verbo em -ing = passado perfeito contínuo, voz ativa: é a areia que “vinha se acumulando”. É esta a forma que parece passiva: had been seguido de particípio seria passiva, mas aqui vem o gerúndio.

Nas alternativas erradas: (a) erra o item III; (b) erra os itens I, II e III; (d) erra o item I; (e) erra os itens I e II.
questoes.dica: Dica: depois de has/had been, olhe a forma seguinte. Particípio (left, removed) = voz passiva; verbo em -ing (accumulating) = tempo contínuo na voz ativa. O tempo está no primeiro auxiliar: is → presente; has → presente perfeito; had → passado perfeito. Para confirmar a voz, pergunte se o sujeito pratica a ação (a areia acumula) ou a sofre (o flanco foi deixado).

questoes.enunciado: O segmento destacado em “Layer 11, the oldest reliably dated charcoal-bearing layer in the sequence, was modelled to 5,580–5,410 cal BP” (§17) pode ser traduzido, no contexto em que é empregado, por
alternativas: a camada que contém o carvão mais antigo datado de forma confiável.
a camada datada de forma mais confiável entre as que contêm carvão antigo.
a mais antiga das camadas datadas de forma confiável pelo carvão que contêm.
a mais antiga das camadas de carvão datadas de forma confiável.
a mais antiga das camadas com carvão que foram datadas de forma confiável.
questoes.explicacao:
O núcleo é o último substantivo, layer (camada). À esquerda vêm, de fora para dentro: o superlativo oldest (“a mais antiga”), que se aplica à camada; o particípio com advérbio reliably dated (“datada de forma confiável”); e o adjetivo composto charcoal-bearing (“que contém carvão”, “com carvão”). Resultado: (e), a mais antiga entre as camadas que têm carvão e foram datadas com segurança. O §17 confirma: a Camada 11 é a mais baixa da sequência e foi datada por concha e carvão.

(a) desloca oldest para o carvão: o texto fala da camada mais antiga, não do carvão mais antigo. (b) transforma oldest em “antigo” do carvão e cria um superlativo para reliably (“mais confiável”) que não existe. (c) lê charcoal-bearing como “datada pelo carvão”; -bearing significa “que contém, que porta”, e não diz com que material foi datada. (d) faz da camada uma “camada de carvão”, isto é, composta de carvão, quando ela apenas contém carvão (é uma camada de conchas e sedimento).
questoes.dica: Dica: traduza do núcleo (último substantivo) para a esquerda e pergunte a que palavra cada modificador se liga. Superlativos (oldest, most) costumam ir para o núcleo; advérbios em -ly (reliably) modificam o particípio que vem logo depois. Compostos com -ing (charcoal-bearing, shell-rich, fire-cracked) funcionam como um adjetivo só: X-bearing = “que contém X”.

questoes.enunciado: Com base na Tabela 1 (entre o §16 e o §17), é correto afirmar que
alternativas: na camada 11, a concha é cerca de 20 anos mais antiga que o carvão de galhos, diferença pequena, já que os dois intervalos calibrados se sobrepõem.
nas camadas 7 e 9, cujo carvão é de tronco, os intervalos da concha e do carvão não se sobrepõem, e em ambas o carvão é o mais antigo do par.
na camada 4, a diferença de 30 anos mostra que concha e carvão discordam, já que os limites dos dois intervalos calibrados não são os mesmos.
a maior diferença entre concha e carvão está na camada 7, em que o carvão de tronco é cerca de 330 anos mais antigo que a concha do mesmo contexto.
as idades por luminescência da areia logo abaixo da camada 11 coincidem com as das conchas do horizonte natural, de cerca de 7,5 mil anos.
questoes.explicacao:
(b) Camada 7: concha 4,980–4,790, carvão 5,240–5,050; camada 9: concha 5,240–5,060, carvão 5,580–5,380. Nos dois casos, o limite mais recente do carvão (5,050 e 5,380) é mais antigo que o limite mais antigo da concha (4,980 e 5,240): os intervalos não se sobrepõem, e a diferença é negativa (−260 e −330), o que, pela nota, significa that the charcoal is older than the shell. É o que o §15 diz dos dois pares incompatíveis: both trunk-wood ones, and in each of them the charcoal was older than the shell.

(a) inverte a diferença: na camada 11 o valor é −20, ou seja, o carvão é que é 20 anos mais antigo. A sobreposição está certa, mas o sentido da diferença está trocado.

(c) trata sobreposição como diferença: na camada 4 os intervalos (4,150–3,990 e 4,110–3,970) se sobrepõem quase totalmente; limites diferentes não significam discordância.

(d) troca a camada: −330 é a camada 9; a camada 7 tem −260. A afirmação de que é a maior diferença vale para a camada 9.

(e) troca a linha: a areia sob a camada 11 deu 6.0 ± 0.4 e 5.8 ± 0.4 ka; 7.5 ± 0.5 ka é a OSL do horizonte natural de conchas, outra linha da Unidade S0.
questoes.dica: Dica: antes de ler as alternativas, leia o título, o cabeçalho e a nota da tabela: é a nota que diz o que significa o sinal negativo e em que unidade estão os números. Depois confira cada alternativa na linha e na coluna certas. Intervalos que se sobrepõem indicam concordância, mesmo que os limites não sejam idênticos; diferença “de X anos” só tem sentido com a direção (quem é mais antigo).

questoes.enunciado: Assinale a alternativa que apresenta uma informação FALSA de acordo com o texto.
alternativas: Mesmo depois de calibradas com a curva marinha e o ΔR regional, as datas de concha continuaram, em média, cerca de 540 anos mais antigas que as de carvão do mesmo contexto (§15).
Nas três camadas superiores, um terço das datas de radiocarbono contrariava a posição estratigráfica, proporção bem maior que a das camadas 4 a 11 (§14).
Calibradas e corrigidas, as duas conchas do horizonte natural forneceram idades compatíveis com a da amostra de luminescência colhida ao lado delas (§16).
Para os autores, a concha de um bivalve tende a registrar bem o momento do descarte, já que o animal vive poucos anos e provavelmente foi consumido logo após a coleta (§18).
A data obtida em 1987 foi praticamente reproduzida em duas amostras novas, razão pela qual os autores não põem em dúvida a precisão da medição original (§19).
questoes.explicacao:
(a) é a falsa: troca o valor não corrigido pelo corrigido. Os 540 anos são a diferença antes da correção: Before correction, the shell dates were older than the paired charcoal dates in all 14 cases, by a mean of 540 years. Depois dela, the mean difference fell to 115 years (§15).

(b) é verdadeira: Of the nine radiocarbon dates from Layers 1 to 3, three (33%) were inconsistent with their stratigraphic position, contra only one of the 23 dates from Layers 4 to 11 (4%) (§14).

(c) é verdadeira: as conchas, once calibrated with the marine curve and ΔR, correspond to 7,680–7,480 and 7,560–7,360 cal BP, in close agreement with the adjacent OSL age (7.5 ± 0.5 ka) (§16).

(d) é verdadeira, parafraseando A bivalve lives for only a few years and was, in all likelihood, eaten and discarded soon after it was collected (§18).

(e) é verdadeira: its accuracy is scarcely in doubt, since it has now been reproduced on two independent samples (§19).
questoes.dica: Dica: em “assinale a FALSA”, confira cada afirmação no parágrafo indicado e procure o detalhe trocado: antes × depois de uma correção, calibrada × não calibrada, mais antiga × mais recente, qual material. Uma afirmação pode repetir um número correto do texto (como 540) e ainda assim ser falsa, porque o liga à condição errada.

questoes.enunciado: Assinale o segmento em que o termo sublinhado NÃO estabelece relação de CONTRASTE ou oposição.
alternativas: “A bivalve lives for only a few years […]; <u>yet</u> it is precisely this material that sambaqui researchers have tended to distrust” (§18).
“Charcoal from trunk wood, <u>conversely</u>, may incorporate carbon fixed decades or centuries before the fire” (§18).
“the lower six layers […] accumulated within roughly 600 years, and the remaining 3.8 m accumulated <u>rather</u> slowly over more than a millennium” (§17).
“<u>Even so</u>, neither explanation alone would account for the full discrepancy” (§19).
“The radiocarbon dates are far more precise than the OSL ages, <u>whereas</u> the OSL ages have the advantage of being entirely independent of carbon” (§20).
questoes.explicacao:
Em (c), rather modifica o advérbio slowly: rather slowly = “bastante devagar”, “um tanto devagar”. É um intensificador (grau), não um conector. A oposição entre as duas partes da frase existe (rápido × devagar), mas quem liga as partes é and; rather só indica o grau da lentidão. Não confunda com rather than (“em vez de”), esse sim de oposição.

Os demais marcam contraste: (a) yet = “no entanto”: a concha tem vida curta e é descartada logo, e mesmo assim é o material de que se desconfia; (b) conversely = “inversamente”, “por outro lado”: opõe o carvão de tronco à concha; (d) even so = “mesmo assim”, contraste concessivo: apesar de as duas explicações terem mérito, nenhuma basta sozinha; (e) whereas = “ao passo que”: opõe a precisão do radiocarbono à independência da luminescência.
questoes.dica: Dica: antes de classificar, veja o que a palavra sublinhada modifica. Se ela vem colada a um adjetivo ou advérbio (rather slowly, fairly, quite), é grau, não conexão entre ideias. Conectores de contraste: yet, however, conversely, on the other hand, in contrast, whereas, even so, nevertheless. Teste a troca por “no entanto/ao passo que”: se a frase perde o sentido, não é contraste.

questoes.enunciado:
Considere os segmentos a seguir.

I - “the deep water that rises to the surface offshore may have been isolated from it for centuries” (§7)II - “The mound, which formerly rose some 12 m above the lagoon shore, now reaches about 9 m” (§10)III - “Because charcoal was distributed unevenly through the sequence, paired shell and charcoal samples […] could be obtained in only 14 cases” (§11)IV - “indeed, its accuracy is scarcely in doubt, since it has now been reproduced on two independent samples” (§19)

Os segmentos sublinhados apresentam, respectivamente, ideia de
alternativas: frequência – lugar – intensidade – modo.
frequência – tempo – intensidade – tempo.
frequência – tempo – modo – intensidade.
lugar – lugar – intensidade – intensidade.
lugar – tempo – modo – intensidade.
questoes.explicacao:
I offshore = “ao largo”, “longe da costa, em mar aberto”: diz onde a água profunda sobe à superfície → lugar.

II formerly = “antigamente”, “outrora”: situa a altura de 12 m num momento anterior, em oposição a now → tempo. O -ly não o torna advérbio de modo.

III unevenly = “de forma desigual”, “irregularmente”: diz como o carvão estava distribuído → modo. A ideia de lugar está em through the sequence, não no advérbio; e o advérbio não mede quanto carvão havia.

IV scarcely = “mal”, “quase não”: gradua o quanto a exatidão está em dúvida (quase nada) → intensidade. Não é frequência: não significa “raramente” neste trecho, já que não há ação repetida.

Nas alternativas erradas: (a) erra os itens I, II, III e IV; (b) erra os itens I, III e IV; (c) erra o item I; (d) erra os itens II e III.
questoes.dica: Dica: classifique o advérbio pela pergunta que ele responde no trecho: onde? (lugar: offshore, upslope, inland), quando? (tempo: formerly, hitherto, now), como? (modo: unevenly, gradually), em que grau? (intensidade: scarcely, barely, largely), com que frequência? (seldom, routinely). Não se guie pelo sufixo -ly nem pelas palavras vizinhas (through the sequence é lugar, mas não é o termo sublinhado).

questoes.enunciado: No §19, depois de afirmar que as conchas datadas em 1987 provavelmente vinham do horizonte natural de conchas, e não das camadas do sambaqui, os autores escrevem: “This is not to say that the original measurement was flawed; indeed, its accuracy is scarcely in doubt” (§19). A função do segmento sublinhado é
alternativas: antecipar e afastar uma conclusão indevida que o leitor poderia tirar do que acabou de ser dito: a de que a medição de 1987 estaria errada.
contestar a hipótese de Ferreira-Lund (2009), retomada na frase anterior, de que as conchas datadas não teriam sido descartadas por pessoas.
introduzir uma limitação do próprio estudo, que reconhece não ter conseguido repetir a medição feita sobre as amostras de 1987.
concluir o parágrafo, resumindo numa só frase as explicações de Tessaro e Moyle (2004) e de Ferreira-Lund (2009) para a data.
apresentar uma consequência que decorre de a data antiga ter sido reproduzida em duas amostras novas e independentes do sítio.
questoes.explicacao:
Os autores acabaram de dizer que a data de 1987 não se refere ao sambaqui. Um leitor poderia deduzir que a medição estava errada. This is not to say that… (“Isso não quer dizer que…”) bloqueia essa dedução antes que ela seja feita: a medição era boa (its accuracy is scarcely in doubt); errada foi a inferência (What was mistaken was the inference drawn from it). É uma ressalva que antecipa uma objeção, (a).

(b) inverte a relação: a frase anterior apoia Ferreira-Lund (as Ferreira-Lund (2009) suspected), e a ressalva não a contesta. (c) confunde ressalva com limitação; a medição, aliás, foi reproduzida (reproduced on two independent samples), e as limitações ficam no §22. (d) O parágrafo não termina aí: continua com What was mistaken… e Even so…. (e) A reprodução em duas amostras é a justificativa da ressalva (since…), não algo que decorre dela.
questoes.dica: Dica: para a função de expressões como This is not to say that…, This does not mean that…, pergunte que conclusão o leitor tiraria da frase anterior e veja se a expressão a nega. Elas limitam o alcance do que foi dito, sem contestar o resultado. Distinga: ressalva (limita a inferência) × contra-argumento (contesta a afirmação) × limitação (fraqueza do próprio estudo).

questoes.enunciado: Assinale a alternativa cujo segmento sublinhado expressa NECESSIDADE, isto é, algo que precisa ser feito, e não uma possibilidade, uma dedução ou um grau de certeza.
alternativas: “in estuarine settings the offset <u>may</u> vary with the amount of freshwater input” (§22).
“Such dates <u>need to</u> be recalibrated with an appropriate ΔR” (§21).
“A backfilled pit, which <u>must have</u> been dug after the 1950s, since its fill contained fragments of plastic” (§10).
“Single-grain OSL dating of the shell-bearing sediment itself […] <u>might</u> provide an independent age for each layer” (§23).
“the basal date of 7,180 BP, far from marking the arrival of the mound builders, <u>almost certainly</u> records a natural shell bed” (§24).
questoes.explicacao:
Need to + verbo (“precisam ser recalibradas”) expressa necessidade: as datas antigas de concha sem correção têm de ser recalibradas antes de servir de argumento (§21). É (b).

(c) é a armadilha: must costuma ser associado a obrigação, mas must have + particípio é dedução sobre o passado: a cova “deve ter sido” cavada depois de 1950, conclusão tirada do plástico no preenchimento. Ninguém está obrigado a nada. (a) may e (d) might indicam possibilidade. (e) almost certainly marca alto grau de certeza, não necessidade.
questoes.dica: Dica: distinga as famílias. Necessidade/obrigação: need to, have to, is required to, it is essential that, must + infinitivo (no sentido de dever). Dedução: must have + particípio, can only be. Possibilidade: may, might, could. Certeza: almost certainly, clearly, undoubtedly. Pergunte: o trecho diz o que tem de ser feito ou o que provavelmente é/foi o caso?

questoes.enunciado: Com base no segmento “A local ΔR value could be obtained by dating shells of known collection date held in museum collections gathered from the lagoon before nuclear weapons testing altered atmospheric carbon-14 in the 1950s” (§23), pode-se inferir que
alternativas: o ΔR aplicado neste estudo já havia sido calculado a partir de conchas de museu da própria laguna, coletadas antes dos testes nucleares.
as conchas de museu permitiriam datar diretamente as camadas do sambaqui, dispensando o radiocarbono das amostras escavadas no sítio.
os testes nucleares alteraram o carbono-14 da atmosfera e, por isso, tornam inválidas todas as datas de radiocarbono medidas depois de 1950.
conchas recolhidas na laguna depois da década de 1950 não serviriam para esse cálculo, pois o seu carbono-14 refletiria a alteração causada pelos testes.
a extração de cal da década de 1950 alterou o carbono-14 das conchas do próprio sítio, o que torna indispensável um ΔR local para corrigi-las.
questoes.explicacao:
(d) O trecho exige duas condições para as conchas de museu: data de coleta conhecida e coleta before nuclear weapons testing altered atmospheric carbon-14 in the 1950s. Se a restrição existe, é porque conchas posteriores teriam carbono-14 alterado e não mostrariam o efeito reservatório natural. O texto não diz isso literalmente, mas o autoriza.

(a) contradiz o texto: o ΔR usado foi regional rather than specific to the Taquarema lagoon (§22), tirado de Nakamura-Reis (2015) (§12). Obter um valor local é justamente a proposta para o futuro.

(b) generaliza demais: as conchas de museu serviriam para calibrar a correção (o ΔR), não para datar as camadas; o radiocarbono das amostras continua necessário.

(c) é a leitura apressada: o que os testes alteraram foi o carbono-14 incorporado por organismos que viveram depois deles. O texto não diz que medições feitas depois de 1950 sejam inválidas; as datas do próprio estudo foram medidas em 2023–2024.

(e) mistura duas informações da mesma década: a extração de cal dos anos 1950 (§10) destruiu metade do sambaqui, mas não tem relação com o carbono-14; quem o alterou foram os testes nucleares.
questoes.dica: Dica: numa inferência, pergunte por que o autor impõe cada condição (“de data conhecida”, “antes de…”): a resposta costuma ser a conclusão não dita. Descarte o que só se apoia numa palavra do trecho (1950, conchas), o que contradiz outro parágrafo e o que estende a ideia para “todas” as datas ou “dispensa” um método.

questoes.enunciado: No segmento “No single method, however, would have been sufficient: it was only by dating different materials from the same contexts, by checking them against luminescence ages and by combining all of them with the stratigraphic order that the biases of each method could be identified. The chronologies of other shell middens, many of which rest on a single uncorrected date, should be revisited in the same way” (§24), o segmento destacado refere-se a
alternativas: “by dating different materials from the same contexts, by checking them against luminescence ages and by combining all of them with the stratigraphic order” (§24).
“the biases of each method could be identified” (§24).
“by checking them against luminescence ages” (§24).
“by dating different materials from the same contexts” (§24).
Todo o conteúdo do §23.
questoes.explicacao:
In the same way (“da mesma maneira”) retoma um modo de fazer já descrito. A frase anterior descreve como este estudo chegou ao resultado: it was only by dating different materials from the same contexts, by checking them against luminescence ages and by combining all of them with the stratigraphic order. Os três by + -ing formam um único procedimento, e a recomendação é revisar as cronologias de outros sambaquis seguindo esse procedimento completo — justamente porque No single method […] would have been sufficient.

(b) é a leitura apressada (o trecho imediatamente anterior), mas é o resultado do procedimento, não uma maneira de revisar cronologias. (c) e (d) são só uma parte do que é retomado; escolher uma etapa isolada contradiz a própria frase, que diz que nenhum método sozinho bastaria. (e) está em outro parágrafo e reúne propostas para o futuro (ΔR local, carvão de vida curta, OSL de grão único), que este estudo não aplicou; a expressão aponta para o que o estudo fez, descrito na frase anterior do §24.
questoes.dica: Dica: in the same way, likewise e do the same retomam um procedimento, não um resultado. Procure na frase anterior a descrição de como algo foi feito (muitas vezes uma série de by + -ing) e confira se a alternativa traz o procedimento inteiro ou só uma parte dele.
